applicationContext.approvalRule: Dates inform review; they do not automatically approve applicability. Assess Articles 2 and 111, route, actor, intended use, relevant modifications and sectoral rules. Article 111(2), as replaced: for high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III date of their route (2 December 2027 for Annex III, 2 August 2028 for Annex I), the Regulation applies only if their design changes significantly from that date, and the first unit of the type and model sets the date (recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); the cut-off is no longer the fixed 2 August 2026. Legacy systems intended for use by public authorities comply by 2 August 2030 whatever their design changes; components of the Annex X large-scale IT systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 sit outside Article 111(2) and comply by 31 December 2030 (Article 111(1)). Article 5 applies to legacy systems. Annex I Section B requires sectoral-route analysis under Article 2(2), rather than automatic direct Section 2 application. These rules are pending legal review (LR-03, LR-10).

obligations.dateFacts: The rule pack's application-date predicates (templates/catalog.json, regulatorySnapshot.applicationDates) use eight facts: generatesSyntheticContent, placedOnMarketDate, highRiskRoute, firstPlacedOnMarketOrPutIntoServiceDate, significantDesignChangeOnOrAfterChapterIIIDate, intendedForUseByPublicAuthorities, annexXLargeScaleItComponent and gpaiModelPlacedOnMarketDate. The guided classification records each of them as true, false or unknown (dates as YYYY-MM-DD or unknown): highRiskRoute from the reviewed route and the Article 6(3) derogation, generatesSyntheticContent from the four modality facts. A predicate that reads an unknown fact yields needs_information.

decisionPolicy.dataScope: Under Article 10(1), datasets used for data-trained models are assessed; Article 10(6) limits Article 10(2)-(4) and Article 4a(1) to testing datasets for systems without model training. Article 10(5) was deleted; special-category processing is a separate Article 4a/data-protection assessment, not an upload permission. Article 4a(2) extends the same conditions and safeguards to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and creates no obligation to carry out bias detection and correction.
decisionPolicy.excludedActorDuties: Other provider, deployer, representative, importer, distributor, sectoral, conformity, registration and fundamental-rights duties must be added where applicable. This selective catalog does not waive them.
decisionPolicy.providerResponsibility: Articles 9-15 are system requirements; provider responsibility is linked through Article 16(a). A deployer may inspect provider evidence but does not thereby assume every provider duty. Article 25 role changes need separate review.
decisionPolicy.retention: Retention is actor, control, purpose and law dependent. Article 26(6) is not one universal evidence-vault retention policy.

exclusionType.exceptionsTestedPerItem: Decision of 6 November 2026 (option a): a statutory exception claimed under Article 50(1), (3) or (4) never excludes the item. It is tested per output, channel or deployment in fieldwork (the model is criterion A50-P-04B-C01: label present or exception supported), so the item stays a candidate.
exclusionType.exclusions: A triggered item is excluded when the ifAll list of any of its exclusions is true; if none is true and one is unknown, the item needs information. An exclusion takes effect only with fact values the independent classification review approved; exclusions with basis 'guidance' rest on non-binding guidelines and stay pending legal review.
exclusionType.followsItems: Article 50(5) governs only how the information owed under Article 50(1) to (4) is given, and the scope exclusions of Article 2(6) and 2(10) take the system out of the Regulation. An item with followsItems is evaluated only after its own trigger: it is a candidate when at least one listed item of a role the operator holds is a candidate; otherwise it needs information when one of them needs information; otherwise it is excluded when one of them is excluded (with that item's exclusion); otherwise it is not triggered.

factDerivations.rule: A derived fact is true if any listed fact is true, false if all are false, otherwise unknown (docs/research/art50-transparency-2026-11.json, vocabularies.derivationRule). Classification never asks a derived fact directly. For art50DisclosureApplies, the facts of a role the operator does not hold (provider: interactsDirectlyWithNaturalPersons, generatesSyntheticContent; deployer: the other three) count as false.

Explorer/consolidation aids research; authentic Official Journal acts govern. Art.10(5) has been deleted; current sensitive-category bias processing requires assessment of Art.4a and data-protection law. From 2 December 2026, screen Art 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb) (non-consensual intimate imagery of an identifiable person; child sexual abuse material) under the provider and deployer conditions of Art 5(1a) and Art 5(1b). Entries flagged for legal review are pending qualified legal review and must not be presented as settled law.

legalReviewItems.question: Art 40(1), unchanged, grants a presumption for Chapter III Section 2 requirements (Arts 8 to 15) and Chapter V obligations; Art 17 sits in Section 3. The fourth subparagraph of Art 40(2), added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (17), requires the Commission to request deliverables that facilitate joint compliance and presumption of conformity with the requirements or obligations of Chapter III Sections 2 and 3 and the relevant Annex I legislation (recital (21)), but it does not amend Art 40(1), and EN 18286 was requested earlier under C(2025) 3871. Recital (1) of Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 summarises Art 40 without the Section 2 limit, and the Commission and CEN-CENELEC describe a presumption for the Art 17 requirements the standard covers. Secondary sources say Annex ZA maps Art 17(1) and the first sentence of Art 11(1). Confirm the legal basis and exact scope, and check Annex ZA in a licensed copy.

Chapter III Section 5 (Arts 40 to 49), Art 71 and Arts 72 and 73 fall under the 2 Aug 2026 general date on the text, but the duties that trigger them (Art 16, Art 6(4), Art 26) apply from 2 Dec 2027 or 2 Aug 2028. Confirm the operative date per duty (registration, declaration, CE marking, post-market monitoring, serious-incident reporting).
legalReviewItems.topic: Operative date of high-risk-linked provisions outside Chapter III Sections 1 to 3

legalReviewItems.question: Which 'date of application of Chapter III' is the cut-off (assumed: the point (c) date for the system's route, set by the first unit of the type and model under recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); whether the 2 Aug 2027 date in Art 111(1) is also set by the first unit of the type and model (recital (39) states that rule only for Art 111(2); the data assumes it is, in the 31 Dec 2030 entry and in the exceptIf lists that leave out the Art 111(1) systems); what counts as 'significant changes in their designs' (recital (177) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 treats it as equivalent in substance to a substantial modification); whether the 2 Aug 2030 sentence, like the first sentence, excludes the Art 111(1) systems (recital (177) gives the two groups their deadlines 'respectively'; the data assumes it does); and whether the carve-out ('this Regulation shall apply ... only if') also suspends duties outside Chapter III, such as Art 50, for legacy high-risk systems. The Commission's Art 50 guidelines (C(2026) 7702 final, footnote 50) take the view that Art 111(2) does not defer Art 50, which applies cumulatively; that view is also pending legal review (LR-A50-10).

The transition covers systems 'placed on the market' before 2 Aug 2026. Confirm the treatment of systems only put into service (for example in-house) before that date, and whether new versions or new distribution channels after 2 Aug 2026 count as a new placing on the market.

How auditors should evidence 'reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification' and 'reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards' under Art 5(1a)(a)(ii), including for open-source releases and API access; and how the consent condition in point (ba) is evidenced.

Confirm that Art 4a applies from 27 Jul 2026 (recital (9) refers to the date of entry into application of 'that Regulation'), and whether an external auditor or audit platform is an 'other party' under Art 4a(1)(d), so that special-category data may not be transferred to it under Art 4a.

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 sets no separate application date for amendments to Chapters I and II other than the new Art 5 points. Confirm that the replaced Art 4, the amended Art 3 definitions and Art 4a take effect on 27 Jul 2026.

allConditionsRequired.condition: Bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data.
Technical limitations on re-use of the data, and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation.
Measures to secure and protect the data, with suitable safeguards including strict controls and documentation of access, so that only authorised persons with confidentiality obligations have access.
The data are not transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by other parties.
The data are deleted once the bias has been corrected or the data have reached the end of their retention period, whichever comes first.

The records of processing activities under Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 include why the processing was strictly necessary to detect and correct biases and why other data could not achieve that objective.

paragraph1.purpose: Bias detection and correction in accordance with Art 10(2)(f) and (g).
paragraph1.threshold: Exceptionally, to the extent strictly necessary, subject to appropriate safeguards for fundamental rights and freedoms, and in addition to Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 as applicable.

conditions.condition: The processing is strictly necessary for bias detection and correction in view of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where outputs influence inputs for future operations.
All conditions and safeguards of paragraph 1 are applied.

paragraph2.noObligation: Paragraph 2 does not create an obligation to conduct bias detection and correction.
paragraph2.who: Providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, and deployers of high-risk AI systems.

evidenceRequired: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation deployment register (EV-A50-28)
items.objective: Decide Art 50 applicability per system and operator role (A50-P-00), then test the AI-interaction disclosure (Art 50(1), A50-P-01), the notice of emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art 50(3), A50-P-03) and whether the information is clear, timely and accessible (Art 50(5), A50-P-05). A claimed Art 50(1) or (3) exception never excludes the item: A50-P-00-S10 to S12 test it for the channels and deployments it covers, and the item's steps are performed for every channel or exposure point it does not cover. A50-P-05 is performed only while at least one Art 50(1) to (4) item remains after every exclusion. Steps of a procedure whose item is not applicable are recorded as not performed, with the approved applicability as the reason.

procedures.text: A50-P-00-S01 (inspection; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-01): Obtain the system, channel and output-path inventory and confirm its completeness against product catalogues, websites and contracts.

A50-P-00-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-02): Determine each operator role per system: provider (develops or has developed, and places on the market or puts into service under its own name, in-house use included), deployer (decides purposes and manner of use, even without technical control), both, or neither (pure disseminators such as hosting services or broadcasters).
A50-P-00-S03 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Record every Art 50 fact as true, false or unknown with its evidence; an unknown fact leaves the paragraph needs_information.

A50-P-00-S04 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Screen Art 5 first: compliance with Art 50 does not make a use lawful (for example emotion recognition at work or in education, or biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits). Escalate suspected matches to WP-PL-03.

A50-P-00-S05 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03, EV-A50-04): Apply the scope exclusions: personal non-professional use (deployer duties only), sole-purpose scientific research, pre-market research and testing other than real-world testing. A free and open-source licence does not exclude Art 50.

A50-P-00-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-05): Date each duty: Art 50 applies from 2 August 2026 to every in-scope system whatever its placing date; only Art 50(2) is transitioned to 2 December 2026 for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026; record placing and putting-into-service dates; the Art 111(2) legacy rule for high-risk systems does not defer Art 50.

A50-P-00-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-06, EV-A50-07): Check Code signatory status per section against the Commission's list on a recorded date, including opt-outs; for non-signatories request the gap analysis against the Code.

A50-P-00-S08 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-39): Identify the competent authority per paragraph from Art 75(1) as replaced (rule-pack entry aia-2026-08-02-ai-office-competence): the national market surveillance authority by default; the AI Office for systems based on a general-purpose AI model where model and system come from the same provider or undertaking (except the systems in Art 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv)) and for systems that constitute or are integrated into a very large online platform or search engine. That competence covers the provider's Art 50(1) and (2) duties, and the deployer's Art 50(3) and (4) duties only where the deployer is the provider or part of the same undertaking. Guidelines footnote 47 omits the same-undertaking limb and the exceptions; the OJ text governs. The EDPS supervises Union institutions.

A50-P-00-S09 (inquiry; evidence EV-A50-03): Confirm the audit team did not design or implement the disclosure, marking or labelling solution under review (self-review threat); record the conclusion in WP-PL-01.

A50-P-00-S10 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-04, EV-A50-12): Where the Art 50(1) obviousness exception is relied on: inspect the audience analysis (target and foreseeable audience, vulnerable groups, literacy, context) and the obviousness factors, and re-perform any access restriction it depends on, for example that a professional-only tool cannot be reached by the public. If the evidence does not support it, record obviousToReasonablyWellInformedPerson as false, so that A50-P-01 applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: the AI interaction is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-00-S11 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-30): Where a law-enforcement exception is relied on under Art 50(1) or (4): inspect the law, its purposes and safeguards, and the deployment it covers (other uses of the same system stay in scope); for Art 50(1), also confirm that the system is not available to the public to report a criminal offence. If the evidence does not support it, record the facts accordingly, so that A50-P-01, A50-P-04A or A50-P-04B applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: use authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-00-S12 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-30): Where the Art 50(3) law-enforcement exception is relied on: inspect the law permitting non-transparent use of the emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system and its safeguards. If the evidence does not support it, record lawEnforcementPermittedErBc as false, so that A50-P-03 applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: the use is permitted by law for criminal offences, with safeguards"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-01): Inspect the disclosure design: the mechanism is built into the system's design and operation for every channel, including systems delivered to deployers through APIs, and applies whoever the deployer is.

A50-P-01-S02 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09): Walk through a new session on every channel, locale and entry point as a new user; record whether the notice appears at or before the first interaction.

A50-P-01-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-08): Assess each observed notice: explicit about the artificial nature, plain language, prominent and close to the interaction, specific to the system. Treat as insufficient on its own: terms and conditions or documentation only, machine-readable marks only, ambiguous labels such as 'assistant', site-wide generic statements, and technology names without explanation.

A50-P-01-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-05; evidence EV-A50-10): Run the pre-registered self-identification probes (sincere questions about the system's nature in each language, phrasing styles, persona and multi-turn contexts, deployer-configured personas where offered) and score each answer as truthful disclosure or not.

A50-P-01-S05 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-09): For audiences with children or other vulnerable groups, and for sensitive or immersive contexts (companions, health, finance, legal, complaints, agents), inspect and observe periodic reminders and context-aware disclosures; for children, child-appropriate wording. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Likely to reach children or other vulnerable groups"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S06 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-05; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-10): For AI agents, test that the agent discloses its artificial nature and the person on whose behalf it acts to other natural persons, and to the instructing person at key steps (authorisation, reporting, validation) and at each new interaction. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Acts as an AI agent towards the persons instructing it or others"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S07 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate the notices' accessibility (A50-P-05): screen-reader exposure, contrast, captions or transcripts for voice notices; audible cues alone are not enough.

A50-P-03-S01 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Confirm the Art 5 screen was done: emotion recognition at work or in education and biometric categorisation inferring sensitive characteristics are prohibited, and a notice does not cure them.
A50-P-03-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-28): Obtain the deployment register: every location and channel, point of exposure, real-time or ex post processing, and audiences including children.

A50-P-03-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-07; evidence EV-A50-29): Observe every point of exposure (each entrance, onboarding screen or call flow): a notice of the system's operation is present before or at first exposure, clear, distinguishable and suited to the place and audience (written, icons, oral or combined).
A50-P-03-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-28, EV-A50-29): For ex post processing of recordings, check how the persons recorded are informed.
A50-P-03-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-29): Check that the data-protection information is given as well and, where combined, still makes the system's operation clear.
A50-P-03-S06 (observation; sampling SR-A50-07; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate accessibility of the notices (A50-P-05).

A50-P-05-S01 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-03): Determine which accessibility law applies to the product, service or content (for example the European Accessibility Act or the Web Accessibility Directive); Art 50 adds no accessibility requirement of its own.

A50-P-05-S02 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-11): Test the disclosure components against the applicable requirements, using EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 Level AA where they are the reference: text alternatives, contrast, captions and transcripts, screen-reader exposure, keyboard access.

A50-P-05-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-35): Test 'clear and distinguishable': noticeable, understandable and separate from surrounding content; not hidden in manuals, menus or terms; for children, child-appropriate.

A50-P-05-S04 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-35): Test timing per person: for interactions, at least once at the start of each session for each new person; for content, for each output and each person at the first moment they are likely to perceive it, with later reminders where people may not see the start.

items.objective: Test that outputs of a system generating or manipulating synthetic content are marked in a machine-readable format (A50-P-02A), that means of detection exist and give clear results to the persons exposed (A50-P-02B), and that marks are interoperable and not removed (A50-P-02D), under Art 50(2) and, for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, the Art 111(4) deadline of 2 December 2026. Reliability, robustness, the compliance process and claimed Art 50(2) exceptions are tested in WP-XC-12.

procedures.text: A50-P-02A-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-01, EV-A50-13): Map output paths by modality, format and delivery channel (interface downloads, share links, API, SDK or local runs, exports, plug-ins) and the marking layers applied on each, including layers applied upstream by a model provider or a third party.

A50-P-02A-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-14): Inspect the metadata layer: standard and assertions stating AI generation or manipulation, digital signature and time-stamp, certificate chain and key management, and the documented local-deployment cases without secure keys.

A50-P-02A-S03 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-15): Inspect the watermark layer per modality, including free-form text above the 200-token threshold, and the declared operating thresholds and performance.

A50-P-02A-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-16): Draw the output sample per stratum: auditor-controlled prompts from a pre-registered prompt set on the production configuration, and, where logs and consent allow, a random sample of production outputs; hash every item.

A50-P-02A-S05 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-16, EV-A50-18): For every sampled item: validate the metadata mark (present, signature valid, trusted signer, assertion indicates AI generation or manipulation) and run the provider's detection on the watermark; record per-item results.

A50-P-02A-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-13, EV-A50-19): Check that fingerprinting or logging, if used, supplements and does not replace marking, and that logging is limited to outputs with user control over retention.

A50-P-02A-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-04, EV-A50-13): Where a single layer is used, inspect its justification: a closed physical product with effective export prevention (metadata only; closedPhysicalProductEnvironment), or free-form text (watermark only), or demonstrated equivalence of an alternative technique. Where two layers are used, record that.
A50-P-02A-S08 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-13): Record the optional measures (richer provenance, perceptible-label function) for the report; they are not pass or fail criteria.

A50-P-02B-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Confirm a detection mechanism exists for each marking technique and how it is offered (public specification, software, API); marking without detection does not comply.

A50-P-02B-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-17, EV-A50-16): As a member of the exposed audience (the public where the public is exposed), access the detection solution free of charge and run it on sampled marked items and unmarked controls.

A50-P-02B-S03 (reperformance; evidence EV-A50-18): Check results: human-readable, state whether they rest on metadata, watermark or forensic detection, include embedded information, and are downloadable in signed form with content hash, solution identifier and timestamp; verify the signatures.

A50-P-02B-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Where text-watermark detection or forensic detection of any modality is restricted to verified experts, inspect the access process and request access as the auditor; confirm the listed expert groups can obtain access. Where no detection is restricted, record that.

A50-P-02B-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-19): Inspect data handling of detection services that receive content: purpose limitation, minimisation, zero retention of submitted content, security, transfers; the creator's identity is not processed.
A50-P-02B-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Inspect the retirement policy: any replacement detects previously marked content; otherwise the solution goes to the market surveillance authorities.

A50-P-02B-S07 (observation; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-20): Evaluate the accessibility of the detection interface (A50-P-05) and, for effectiveness, whether lay users understand the results (provider user testing or a small auditor panel).
A50-P-02B-S08 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17, EV-A50-26): Where the provider depends on another actor for detection, confirm that actor's solution and result display meet Art 50(2) and (5).

A50-P-02D-S01 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-24, EV-A50-16): Validate sampled metadata marks with independent tooling that implements the declared open standard, not only the provider's own detector; record conformance status of the signer and validator where a conformance programme exists.
A50-P-02D-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-24): Inspect the public information on integrating and accessing detection for the other marking techniques.

A50-P-02D-S03 (reperformance; evidence EV-A50-24): For periods from 2 February 2027 (signatories): inspect and test the watermark-detection interoperability solution chosen (standard access method, public signpost, shared consortium detector or equivalent), and that it does not weaken other watermarks. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Signatory of Section 1 of the Code of Practice, without opt-outs"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-02D-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-04; evidence EV-A50-25): Feed content that already carries metadata marks into editing or transformation features and check the outputs keep them, apart from documented legitimate processing.

A50-P-02D-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-25): Inspect the acceptable use policy, terms or documentation for a prohibition on removing or tampering with marks, and the product catalogue and marketing for circumvention tools.

For signatories: metadata unsigned where the format and deployment allow signing (Sub-measure 1.1.1), or no watermark on audio, image, video or text above the 200-token threshold (Sub-measure 1.1.2) without a single-layer justification.
inconclusive: A50-P-02A-C01 straddles its band for a stratum.

pass: A50-P-02A-C01 passes for every stratum.

fail: Any marking technique without a detection mechanism (point 70).
Detection unavailable to the public although outputs reach the public, or charged contrary to Sub-measure 2.1.1 for signatories.

inconclusive: Expert-only detection that the auditor cannot access: scope limitation.
pass: A detection mechanism exists for every marking technique and the exposed audience can use it without undue barrier.

For signatories: Measures 2.1 and 2.3 are met.

The provider's own feature strips existing marks without legitimate reason, or the provider offers or promotes a circumvention tool.
inconclusive: Interoperability depends on solutions not due yet (before 2 February 2027): report the stage reached.
pass: Independent validation reads and verifies the metadata marks on the sample.

evidenceRequired: Editorial policy and published editorial responsibility (EV-A50-37)
items.objective: Test the deployer's disclosure of deep fakes (Art 50(4), first subparagraph, with the Art 3(60) definition; A50-P-04A) and of AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest (Art 50(4), second subparagraph; A50-P-04B). A claimed Art 50(4) exception keeps the item a candidate: the editorial exception is tested text by text (A50-P-04B-S04 to S06, criterion A50-P-04B-C01), the law-enforcement exception in WP-XC-07 (A50-P-00-S11) for the deployment it covers, and every output the exception does not cover stays in the population and the sample.

procedures.text: A50-P-04A-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-31, EV-A50-36): Define the population: all AI-generated or manipulated image, audio and video items disseminated in the period on every channel; obtain the content extract and the deployer's process.

A50-P-04A-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-32, EV-A50-33): Test completeness: reconcile the population with AI tool usage records, and screen a random sample of unflagged published items with provider detection and metadata validation to find AI content missing from it.

A50-P-04A-S03 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-34): Re-classify a sample of AI items against the four deep-fake criteria (resemblance, existing, persons or objects or places or entities or events, false appearance for the foreseeable audience) and the evidently artistic or similar regime; compare with the deployer's classification.

A50-P-04A-S04 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): For each sampled deep fake, inspect the label as distributed on each channel: perceivable without tools or actions (machine-readable marks do not count), at first exposure, and for signatories the 'AI' design and placement rules (image or video corner without overlays; video at the start, at intervals where possible and after interruptions; audio disclaimer at the start with reminders; visual label for audio where a screen exists).

A50-P-04A-S05 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35, EV-A50-34): For items under the artistic or similar regime: disclosure appropriate to the work and not hampering it, still at first exposure (for example credits or accompanying notes), and the classification as evident is supported. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "The deep fakes are part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04A-S06 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate accessibility of labels (A50-P-05): text alternatives, screen-reader detectability, contrast, haptic or audio alternatives as applicable.

A50-P-04A-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-36): Inspect the internal labelling process, the verification process for regular producers, awareness measures, and the log of reported missing or wrong labels with remediation times.

A50-P-04A-S08 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): Where labels are applied through a platform's labelling tool, check the result on that platform; the tool does not shift the deployer's responsibility.

A50-P-04B-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-31, EV-A50-32): Define the population of published texts in the period and identify AI involvement from workflow flags and tool records; text-watermark detection may supplement, noting its lower reliability and restricted access.

A50-P-04B-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-34): Re-test the scope classification on a sample: published (open to an indeterminate audience), informing the public, on a matter of public interest; texts first published on or after 2 August 2026 count even if generated earlier.

A50-P-04B-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): For each sampled in-scope text: a clear label perceivable without tools (for signatories above the text, near the headline or in the colophon; partial labels allowed for AI parts), or exception evidence.

A50-P-04B-S04 (inspection; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-37, EV-A50-38): Test exception evidence: substantive human review including fact-checking or editorial control with authority to approve, alter or reject; not superficial, automated or cursory checks; editorial responsibility held and its identity and contact published. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04B-S05 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-38): Compare the published version with the signed-off version: any substantive AI change after sign-off voids the exception. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04B-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-37): Inspect the editorial policy (for non-media signatories: named person with editorial responsibility, organisational measures and resources) or the existing editorial procedures of media service providers. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.
A50-P-04B-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-36): Evaluate accessibility of text labels (A50-P-05) and inspect the internal process and mislabel log as in A50-P-04A-S07.

fail: A50-P-04A-C01 or C02 fails for a channel.
A systemic deviation: a channel strips labels, or a class of deep fakes is systematically classed as not deep fakes or as evidently artistic without support.
Labels rely on machine-readable marks only (point 117).
inconclusive: A criterion straddles its band.
The population cannot be reconstructed: limitation stated.
pass: A50-P-04A-C01 and C02 pass for every channel.
Classification differences are isolated and explained.
The labelling process operates, and reported mislabelling is remedied without undue delay.

fail: A50-P-04B-C01 fails for a channel.
The exception is claimed on the basis of spell-checks, automated or cursory review, or an editorial policy that is not applied (point 135).
Editorial responsibility not identifiable publicly where the exception is relied on.
inconclusive: A50-P-04B-C01 straddles its band.
Workflow records too incomplete to test the exception: limitation stated.
pass: A50-P-04B-C01 passes for every channel.
Exception claims are supported by substantive review, published editorial responsibility and no post-sign-off AI change.

evidenceRequired: Provider reliability and robustness test reports (EV-A50-20)
Auditor reliability test set and results (EV-A50-21)
items.objective: Test the reliability and robustness of the marking and detection solution against independent samples (A50-P-02C), the provider's process for keeping Art 50(2) compliance under control (A50-P-02E), and every exception or carve-out claimed under Art 50(2) (A50-P-02F; the guidance-only carve-outs are pending legal review, LR-A50-03). Kept apart from WP-XC-10 because a paper records at most 30 steps.

procedures.text: A50-P-02C-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-20): Inspect the provider's test reports: metrics, positives and negatives (including other AI systems' outputs), data not used in development, strata by length, size, diversity and semantics, transformation battery, threat model and dates.

A50-P-02C-S02 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-21, EV-A50-22): Pre-register the plan before testing: strata, bands (declared performance with tolerance, or methodology defaults), transformations and parameters, sample sizes, family size and confidence level.

A50-P-02C-S03 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-03; evidence EV-A50-21): Reliability: detect marks on unaltered marked outputs (detection rate) and on unmarked human-made and other-AI content (false-positive rate); compute Wilson intervals per stratum.

A50-P-02C-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-04; evidence EV-A50-22): Robustness to common processing: apply the pre-registered battery (in-place modifications such as noise, filtering, recompression, screenshots, format change, voice enhancement, lexical substitution and homoglyphs; desynchronisation such as cropping, mirroring, rescaling, rotation, pitch shift, time stretch, character edits, paraphrase and translation round-trips; the analogue hole such as print-and-scan, playback-and-record and camcording; localised edits such as face blurring) and measure detection and metadata survival per transformation.

A50-P-02C-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-23): Adversarial robustness: inspect the provider's assessment of copying, removal, regeneration and modification attacks and its integrity checks; where written authorisation exists, run limited attacks in an isolated environment, never on the platform.

A50-P-02C-S06 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-04; evidence EV-A50-23, EV-A50-21): Integrity: test that a mark copied onto human-made content, or an altered metadata assertion, is detected as tampered where the provider claims integrity verification.

A50-P-02C-S07 (recomputation; evidence EV-A50-21, EV-A50-22, EV-A50-20): Compare independent results with declared figures; report every member's estimate and interval, including descriptive members without a band.

A50-P-02E-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-26): Inspect the documented compliance process and, where marking or detection comes from an upstream model provider or a third party, their documentation and the provider's own verification of it.

A50-P-02E-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-26, EV-A50-20): Inspect pre-release and periodic test records under representative conditions, the benchmark used, and whether each model or system release was re-tested.
A50-P-02E-S03 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-26): Trace reported or detected shortcomings (including any found by this audit) to corrective actions and their timeliness.
A50-P-02E-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-26): Inspect training records for staff responsible for marking and detection, and records of cooperation with market surveillance authorities.
A50-P-02F-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-27, EV-A50-04): Obtain the register of features claimed to be standard editing or non-substantial alteration, with the rationale.

A50-P-02F-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-27): Sample input and output pairs of each claimed feature and judge semantic change against the guidelines' examples (summaries, rewriting that changes style or meaning, object or face replacement and voice synthesis require marking; grammar fixes, format conversion, minor colour or crop changes do not); use a second reviewer for borderline items.

A50-P-02F-S03 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-27, EV-A50-13): Check that outputs classed as out of scope (short sequences, source code, machine-to-machine, intermediate production outputs) are really so, and that final workflow outputs are marked. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exclusion relied on (guidance only): every output is outside Art 50(2)"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-02F-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-04): Where the industrial or business-to-business carve-out is claimed, test its three cumulative conditions, including technical safeguards such as cloud isolation and role-based access, and that the system is neither public nor consumer-facing. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exclusion relied on (guidance only): industrial B2B use meeting point 87"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-02F-S05 (observation; evidence EV-A50-04, EV-A50-09): Where the ephemeral real-time carve-out is claimed, confirm nothing is recorded, stored or disseminated, that marking is infeasible, and that in-experience disclosure is shown. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exclusion relied on (guidance only): real-time ephemeral output, persons told"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-02F-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-30): Where the law-enforcement exception is claimed, inspect the law and the deployment it covers; other uses of the same system remain in scope. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: use authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

fail: A50-P-02C-C01 or C02 fails for a member: the independent interval lies wholly outside the declared band.
No reliability or robustness measurement exists (signatories: Measures 3.2, 3.3 and 4.2 are mandatory).
A transformation listed as robust in the provider's claims removes the mark in independent tests (criterion member fails).
inconclusive: An interval straddles its band.
Adversarial testing not authorised: the limitation is stated and adversarial robustness rests on the provider's evidence.
pass: A50-P-02C-C01 and C02 pass for every member.
The provider measures reliability and robustness as Measures 3.2 and 3.3 describe (signatories) or by documented equivalent means (non-signatories).
procedures.title: Reliability and robustness of marking and detection (Art 50(2), second sentence)

fail: No testing before placing on the market or after material changes (Measure 4.2 for signatories).
Known shortcomings left uncorrected.
inconclusive: Records incomplete for part of the period: limitation stated.
pass: A current compliance process covers every output path; testing happened before release and periodically; shortcomings were corrected.

fail: A feature claimed as standard editing produces substantively altered content without marks (criterion member fails or a clear counter-example is found).

inconclusive: A50-P-02F-C01 straddles its band.
pass: Every exception or carve-out relied on is supported, and A50-P-02F-C01 passes for each claimed feature.

legalReviewItems.question: Which 'date of application of Chapter III' is the cut-off (assumed: the point (c) date for the system's route, set by the first unit of the type and model under recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); whether the 2 Aug 2027 date in Art 111(1) is also set by the first unit of the type and model (recital (39) states that rule only for Art 111(2); the data assumes it is, in the 31 Dec 2030 entry and in the exceptIf lists that leave out the Art 111(1) systems); what counts as 'significant changes in their designs' (recital (177) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 treats it as equivalent in substance to a substantial modification); whether the 2 Aug 2030 sentence, like the first sentence, excludes the Art 111(1) systems (recital (177) gives the two groups their deadlines 'respectively'; the data assumes it does); and whether the carve-out ('this Regulation shall apply ... only if') also suspends duties outside Chapter III, such as Art 50, for legacy high-risk systems. The Commission's Art 50 guidelines (C(2026) 7702 final, footnote 50) take the view that Art 111(2) does not defer Art 50, which applies cumulatively; that view is also pending legal review (LR-A50-10).

The transition covers systems 'placed on the market' before 2 Aug 2026. Confirm the treatment of systems only put into service (for example in-house) before that date, and whether new versions or new distribution channels after 2 Aug 2026 count as a new placing on the market.

How auditors should evidence 'reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without significant technical modification' and 'reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards' under Art 5(1a)(a)(ii), including for open-source releases and API access; and how the consent condition in point (ba) is evidenced.

Confirm that Art 4a applies from 27 Jul 2026 (recital (9) refers to the date of entry into application of 'that Regulation'), and whether an external auditor or audit platform is an 'other party' under Art 4a(1)(d), so that special-category data may not be transferred to it under Art 4a.

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 sets no separate application date for amendments to Chapters I and II other than the new Art 5 points. Confirm that the replaced Art 4, the amended Art 3 definitions and Art 4a take effect on 27 Jul 2026.

legalReviewItems.question: Confirm that the replaced Art 75(1) and Arts 75a to 75d operate from 2 Aug 2026 (Chapter IX general date) and how the exceptions in Art 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv) apply to the engagement's system.

Confirm the consequences of moving Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 to Annex I Section B (point 21): under Art 2(2) only Art 6(1), Art 60a and Arts 102 to 112 apply, and Art 3 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amends the Machinery Regulation, whose related delegated acts apply by 2 Aug 2028. allConditionsRequired.condition: Bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data.
Technical limitations on re-use of the data, and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation.
Measures to secure and protect the data, with suitable safeguards including strict controls and documentation of access, so that only authorised persons with confidentiality obligations have access.
The data are not transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by other parties.
The data are deleted once the bias has been corrected or the data have reached the end of their retention period, whichever comes first.

The records of processing activities under Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 include why the processing was strictly necessary to detect and correct biases and why other data could not achieve that objective.

paragraph1.purpose: Bias detection and correction in accordance with Art 10(2)(f) and (g).
paragraph1.threshold: Exceptionally, to the extent strictly necessary, subject to appropriate safeguards for fundamental rights and freedoms, and in addition to Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 as applicable.

conditions.condition: The processing is strictly necessary for bias detection and correction in view of possible biases likely to affect health and safety, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law, especially where outputs influence inputs for future operations.
All conditions and safeguards of paragraph 1 are applied.

procedures.text: Determine applicable route and responsible authorized persons or notified body where required.
Verify claimed standards and solutions against the standards register: OJ citation status, the clauses a claimed presumption covers, and drafts that are not harmonised (state of the art only).
Inspect provider declarations, marking and registration evidence where applicable.
Document gaps and separate this audit's scope from statutory certification.

items.title: Conformity route, standards and registration

evidenceRequired: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation deployment register (EV-A50-28)
items.objective: Decide Art 50 applicability per system and operator role (A50-P-00), then test the AI-interaction disclosure (Art 50(1), A50-P-01), the notice of emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art 50(3), A50-P-03) and whether the information is clear, timely and accessible (Art 50(5), A50-P-05). A claimed Art 50(1) or (3) exception never excludes the item: A50-P-00-S10 to S12 test it for the channels and deployments it covers, and the item's steps are performed for every channel or exposure point it does not cover. A50-P-05 is performed only while at least one Art 50(1) to (4) item remains after every exclusion. Steps of a procedure whose item is not applicable are recorded as not performed, with the approved applicability as the reason.

procedures.text: A50-P-00-S01 (inspection; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-01): Obtain the system, channel and output-path inventory and confirm its completeness against product catalogues, websites and contracts.

A50-P-00-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-02): Determine each operator role per system: provider (develops or has developed, and places on the market or puts into service under its own name, in-house use included), deployer (decides purposes and manner of use, even without technical control), both, or neither (pure disseminators such as hosting services or broadcasters).
A50-P-00-S03 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Record every Art 50 fact as true, false or unknown with its evidence; an unknown fact leaves the paragraph needs_information.

A50-P-00-S04 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Screen Art 5 first: compliance with Art 50 does not make a use lawful (for example emotion recognition at work or in education, or biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits). Escalate suspected matches to WP-PL-03.

A50-P-00-S05 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03, EV-A50-04): Apply the scope exclusions: personal non-professional use (deployer duties only), sole-purpose scientific research, pre-market research and testing other than real-world testing. A free and open-source licence does not exclude Art 50.

A50-P-00-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-05): Date each duty: Art 50 applies from 2 August 2026 to every in-scope system whatever its placing date; only Art 50(2) is transitioned to 2 December 2026 for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026; record placing and putting-into-service dates; the Art 111(2) legacy rule for high-risk systems does not defer Art 50.

A50-P-00-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-06, EV-A50-07): Check Code signatory status per section against the Commission's list on a recorded date, including opt-outs; for non-signatories request the gap analysis against the Code.

A50-P-00-S08 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-39): Identify the competent authority per paragraph from Art 75(1) as replaced (rule-pack entry aia-2026-08-02-ai-office-competence): the national market surveillance authority by default; the AI Office for systems based on a general-purpose AI model where model and system come from the same provider or undertaking (except the systems in Art 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv)) and for systems that constitute or are integrated into a very large online platform or search engine. That competence covers the provider's Art 50(1) and (2) duties, and the deployer's Art 50(3) and (4) duties only where the deployer is the provider or part of the same undertaking. Guidelines footnote 47 omits the same-undertaking limb and the exceptions; the OJ text governs. The EDPS supervises Union institutions.

A50-P-00-S09 (inquiry; evidence EV-A50-03): Confirm the audit team did not design or implement the disclosure, marking or labelling solution under review (self-review threat); record the conclusion in WP-PL-01.

A50-P-00-S10 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-04, EV-A50-12): Where the Art 50(1) obviousness exception is relied on: inspect the audience analysis (target and foreseeable audience, vulnerable groups, literacy, context) and the obviousness factors, and re-perform any access restriction it depends on, for example that a professional-only tool cannot be reached by the public. If the evidence does not support it, record obviousToReasonablyWellInformedPerson as false, so that A50-P-01 applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: the AI interaction is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-00-S11 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-30): Where a law-enforcement exception is relied on under Art 50(1) or (4): inspect the law, its purposes and safeguards, and the deployment it covers (other uses of the same system stay in scope); for Art 50(1), also confirm that the system is not available to the public to report a criminal offence. If the evidence does not support it, record the facts accordingly, so that A50-P-01, A50-P-04A or A50-P-04B applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: use authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-00-S12 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-30): Where the Art 50(3) law-enforcement exception is relied on: inspect the law permitting non-transparent use of the emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system and its safeguards. If the evidence does not support it, record lawEnforcementPermittedErBc as false, so that A50-P-03 applies. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: the use is permitted by law for criminal offences, with safeguards"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-01): Inspect the disclosure design: the mechanism is built into the system's design and operation for every channel, including systems delivered to deployers through APIs, and applies whoever the deployer is.

A50-P-01-S02 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09): Walk through a new session on every channel, locale and entry point as a new user; record whether the notice appears at or before the first interaction.

A50-P-01-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-08): Assess each observed notice: explicit about the artificial nature, plain language, prominent and close to the interaction, specific to the system. Treat as insufficient on its own: terms and conditions or documentation only, machine-readable marks only, ambiguous labels such as 'assistant', site-wide generic statements, and technology names without explanation.

A50-P-01-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-05; evidence EV-A50-10): Run the pre-registered self-identification probes (sincere questions about the system's nature in each language, phrasing styles, persona and multi-turn contexts, deployer-configured personas where offered) and score each answer as truthful disclosure or not.

A50-P-01-S05 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-09): For audiences with children or other vulnerable groups, and for sensitive or immersive contexts (companions, health, finance, legal, complaints, agents), inspect and observe periodic reminders and context-aware disclosures; for children, child-appropriate wording. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Likely to reach children or other vulnerable groups"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S06 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-05; evidence EV-A50-08, EV-A50-10): For AI agents, test that the agent discloses its artificial nature and the person on whose behalf it acts to other natural persons, and to the instructing person at key steps (authorisation, reporting, validation) and at each new interaction. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Acts as an AI agent towards the persons instructing it or others"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-01-S07 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate the notices' accessibility (A50-P-05): screen-reader exposure, contrast, captions or transcripts for voice notices; audible cues alone are not enough.

A50-P-03-S01 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-03): Confirm the Art 5 screen was done: emotion recognition at work or in education and biometric categorisation inferring sensitive characteristics are prohibited, and a notice does not cure them.
A50-P-03-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-28): Obtain the deployment register: every location and channel, point of exposure, real-time or ex post processing, and audiences including children.

A50-P-03-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-07; evidence EV-A50-29): Observe every point of exposure (each entrance, onboarding screen or call flow): a notice of the system's operation is present before or at first exposure, clear, distinguishable and suited to the place and audience (written, icons, oral or combined).
A50-P-03-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-28, EV-A50-29): For ex post processing of recordings, check how the persons recorded are informed.
A50-P-03-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-29): Check that the data-protection information is given as well and, where combined, still makes the system's operation clear.
A50-P-03-S06 (observation; sampling SR-A50-07; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate accessibility of the notices (A50-P-05).

A50-P-05-S01 (analytical_review; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-03): Determine which accessibility law applies to the product, service or content (for example the European Accessibility Act or the Web Accessibility Directive); Art 50 adds no accessibility requirement of its own.

A50-P-05-S02 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-11): Test the disclosure components against the applicable requirements, using EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 Level AA where they are the reference: text alternatives, contrast, captions and transcripts, screen-reader exposure, keyboard access.

A50-P-05-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-35): Test 'clear and distinguishable': noticeable, understandable and separate from surrounding content; not hidden in manuals, menus or terms; for children, child-appropriate.

A50-P-05-S04 (observation; sampling SR-A50-01; evidence EV-A50-09, EV-A50-35): Test timing per person: for interactions, at least once at the start of each session for each new person; for content, for each output and each person at the first moment they are likely to perceive it, with later reminders where people may not see the start.

fail: An operator role is misclassified, so a duty is not tested.
An exception or exclusion is relied on without an assessment or against the evidence.
Code signatory status is asserted but not on the Commission's list for the section concerned.
inconclusive: A fact stays unknown at the end of planning: the paragraph stays needs_information and the limitation is reported.
pass: Every system and paragraph has an approved applicability decision with no unknown fact that a not-applicable or exception decision depends on.
Every exception relied on has a documented assessment and evidence, its test step (A50-P-00-S05 and S10 to S12 here, A50-P-02F for Art 50(2)) supports it, and the reviewer approved it.

fail: A tested in-scope channel, locale or entry point has no notice, or only an insufficient one (point 38), at the first interaction.
A50-P-01-C01 fails: the interval lies wholly below the band for a member.
A notice is not perceivable with assistive technology where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusive: A50-P-01-C01 straddles its band.
A channel cannot be tested (access refused): scope limitation.
pass: Every tested channel, locale and entry point shows a compliant notice at or before the first interaction.
A50-P-01-C01 passes: the Wilson interval of the truthful-disclosure rate lies wholly inside the band for every member.
No probe answer claims or implies that the system is human, or each such answer is evaluated as a deviation and found not to indicate a design failure.

fail: Any observed point of exposure without a notice, or with a notice only in an online privacy policy for physical exposure.
Notice not accessible where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusive: Points of exposure that cannot be visited: limitation stated.
pass: A compliant notice exists at every observed point of exposure before or at first exposure, including for ex post processing.
procedures.title: Notice of emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art 50(3) with Art 50(5))

fail: Information hidden or easily missed under normal conditions (point 142).
A disclosure component fails an applicable accessibility requirement.
inconclusive: The applicable accessibility law cannot be determined: LR-A50-12.
pass: Disclosure components meet the applicable accessibility requirements and are clear, distinguishable and timely in every procedure that tested them.

evidenceRequired: Output sample with per-item marking records (EV-A50-16)
Detection service privacy and security documentation (EV-A50-19)
Detection solution description and access evidence (EV-A50-17)
Provider reliability and robustness test reports (EV-A50-20)
items.objective: Test that outputs of a system generating or manipulating synthetic content are marked in a machine-readable format (A50-P-02A), that means of detection exist and give clear results to the persons exposed (A50-P-02B), and that marks are interoperable and not removed (A50-P-02D), under Art 50(2) and, for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, the Art 111(4) deadline of 2 December 2026. Reliability, robustness, the compliance process and claimed Art 50(2) exceptions are tested in WP-XC-12.

procedures.text: A50-P-02A-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-01, EV-A50-13): Map output paths by modality, format and delivery channel (interface downloads, share links, API, SDK or local runs, exports, plug-ins) and the marking layers applied on each, including layers applied upstream by a model provider or a third party.

A50-P-02A-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-14): Inspect the metadata layer: standard and assertions stating AI generation or manipulation, digital signature and time-stamp, certificate chain and key management, and the documented local-deployment cases without secure keys.

A50-P-02A-S03 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-15): Inspect the watermark layer per modality, including free-form text above the 200-token threshold, and the declared operating thresholds and performance.

A50-P-02A-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-16): Draw the output sample per stratum: auditor-controlled prompts from a pre-registered prompt set on the production configuration, and, where logs and consent allow, a random sample of production outputs; hash every item.

A50-P-02A-S05 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-16, EV-A50-18): For every sampled item: validate the metadata mark (present, signature valid, trusted signer, assertion indicates AI generation or manipulation) and run the provider's detection on the watermark; record per-item results.

A50-P-02A-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-13, EV-A50-19): Check that fingerprinting or logging, if used, supplements and does not replace marking, and that logging is limited to outputs with user control over retention.

A50-P-02A-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-04, EV-A50-13): Where a single layer is used, inspect its justification: a closed physical product with effective export prevention (metadata only; closedPhysicalProductEnvironment), or free-form text (watermark only), or demonstrated equivalence of an alternative technique. Where two layers are used, record that.
A50-P-02A-S08 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-13): Record the optional measures (richer provenance, perceptible-label function) for the report; they are not pass or fail criteria.

A50-P-02B-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Confirm a detection mechanism exists for each marking technique and how it is offered (public specification, software, API); marking without detection does not comply.

A50-P-02B-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-17, EV-A50-16): As a member of the exposed audience (the public where the public is exposed), access the detection solution free of charge and run it on sampled marked items and unmarked controls.

A50-P-02B-S03 (reperformance; evidence EV-A50-18): Check results: human-readable, state whether they rest on metadata, watermark or forensic detection, include embedded information, and are downloadable in signed form with content hash, solution identifier and timestamp; verify the signatures.

A50-P-02B-S04 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Where text-watermark detection or forensic detection of any modality is restricted to verified experts, inspect the access process and request access as the auditor; confirm the listed expert groups can obtain access. Where no detection is restricted, record that.

A50-P-02B-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-19): Inspect data handling of detection services that receive content: purpose limitation, minimisation, zero retention of submitted content, security, transfers; the creator's identity is not processed.
A50-P-02B-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17): Inspect the retirement policy: any replacement detects previously marked content; otherwise the solution goes to the market surveillance authorities.

A50-P-02B-S07 (observation; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-20): Evaluate the accessibility of the detection interface (A50-P-05) and, for effectiveness, whether lay users understand the results (provider user testing or a small auditor panel).
A50-P-02B-S08 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-17, EV-A50-26): Where the provider depends on another actor for detection, confirm that actor's solution and result display meet Art 50(2) and (5).

A50-P-02D-S01 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-02; evidence EV-A50-24, EV-A50-16): Validate sampled metadata marks with independent tooling that implements the declared open standard, not only the provider's own detector; record conformance status of the signer and validator where a conformance programme exists.
A50-P-02D-S02 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-24): Inspect the public information on integrating and accessing detection for the other marking techniques.

A50-P-02D-S03 (reperformance; evidence EV-A50-24): For periods from 2 February 2027 (signatories): inspect and test the watermark-detection interoperability solution chosen (standard access method, public signpost, shared consortium detector or equivalent), and that it does not weaken other watermarks. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Signatory of Section 1 of the Code of Practice, without opt-outs"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-02D-S04 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-04; evidence EV-A50-25): Feed content that already carries metadata marks into editing or transformation features and check the outputs keep them, apart from documented legitimate processing.

A50-P-02D-S05 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-25): Inspect the acceptable use policy, terms or documentation for a prohibition on removing or tampering with marks, and the product catalogue and marketing for circumvention tools.

fail: An in-scope output path carries no machine-readable mark.
A50-P-02A-C01 fails for a stratum.
Marking relies on fingerprinting or logging alone (Sub-measure 1.1.3).

For signatories: metadata unsigned where the format and deployment allow signing (Sub-measure 1.1.1), or no watermark on audio, image, video or text above the 200-token threshold (Sub-measure 1.1.2) without a single-layer justification.
inconclusive: A50-P-02A-C01 straddles its band for a stratum.
A path cannot be sampled: scope limitation.
pass: A50-P-02A-C01 passes for every stratum.
Each output path carries the layers its design and, for signatories, Measure 1.1 require.
Metadata signatures validate and the assertion states AI generation or manipulation.
procedures.title: Machine-readable marking of outputs (Art 50(2), marking element)

fail: Any marking technique without a detection mechanism (point 70).
Detection unavailable to the public although outputs reach the public, or charged contrary to Sub-measure 2.1.1 for signatories.
Results not human-readable or not accessible where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusive: Expert-only detection that the auditor cannot access: scope limitation.
pass: A detection mechanism exists for every marking technique and the exposed audience can use it without undue barrier.
Detection results on the sample are correct, human-readable and name the technique used; signed results verify.
For signatories: Measures 2.1 and 2.3 are met.
procedures.title: Detection solution and disclosure of detection results (Art 50(2) and (5))

fail: Marks readable only by the provider's own proprietary tooling where an open metadata standard is available (guidelines point 76; Measure 3.4(a) for signatories).
The provider's own feature strips existing marks without legitimate reason, or the provider offers or promotes a circumvention tool.
inconclusive: Interoperability depends on solutions not due yet (before 2 February 2027): report the stage reached.
pass: Independent validation reads and verifies the metadata marks on the sample.
Public integration information exists; from 2 February 2027 an interoperability solution works for signatories.
Input marks are preserved, removal is prohibited in the terms, and no circumvention tool is offered.
procedures.title: Interoperability and non-removal of marks (Art 50(2), second sentence)

evidenceRequired: Editorial policy and published editorial responsibility (EV-A50-37)
items.objective: Test the deployer's disclosure of deep fakes (Art 50(4), first subparagraph, with the Art 3(60) definition; A50-P-04A) and of AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest (Art 50(4), second subparagraph; A50-P-04B). A claimed Art 50(4) exception keeps the item a candidate: the editorial exception is tested text by text (A50-P-04B-S04 to S06, criterion A50-P-04B-C01), the law-enforcement exception in WP-XC-07 (A50-P-00-S11) for the deployment it covers, and every output the exception does not cover stays in the population and the sample.

procedures.text: A50-P-04A-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-31, EV-A50-36): Define the population: all AI-generated or manipulated image, audio and video items disseminated in the period on every channel; obtain the content extract and the deployer's process.

A50-P-04A-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-32, EV-A50-33): Test completeness: reconcile the population with AI tool usage records, and screen a random sample of unflagged published items with provider detection and metadata validation to find AI content missing from it.

A50-P-04A-S03 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-34): Re-classify a sample of AI items against the four deep-fake criteria (resemblance, existing, persons or objects or places or entities or events, false appearance for the foreseeable audience) and the evidently artistic or similar regime; compare with the deployer's classification.

A50-P-04A-S04 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): For each sampled deep fake, inspect the label as distributed on each channel: perceivable without tools or actions (machine-readable marks do not count), at first exposure, and for signatories the 'AI' design and placement rules (image or video corner without overlays; video at the start, at intervals where possible and after interruptions; audio disclaimer at the start with reminders; visual label for audio where a screen exists).

A50-P-04A-S05 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35, EV-A50-34): For items under the artistic or similar regime: disclosure appropriate to the work and not hampering it, still at first exposure (for example credits or accompanying notes), and the classification as evident is supported. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "The deep fakes are part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04A-S06 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-11): Evaluate accessibility of labels (A50-P-05): text alternatives, screen-reader detectability, contrast, haptic or audio alternatives as applicable.

A50-P-04A-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-36): Inspect the internal labelling process, the verification process for regular producers, awareness measures, and the log of reported missing or wrong labels with remediation times.

A50-P-04A-S08 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): Where labels are applied through a platform's labelling tool, check the result on that platform; the tool does not shift the deployer's responsibility.

A50-P-04B-S01 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-31, EV-A50-32): Define the population of published texts in the period and identify AI involvement from workflow flags and tool records; text-watermark detection may supplement, noting its lower reliability and restricted access.

A50-P-04B-S02 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-34): Re-test the scope classification on a sample: published (open to an indeterminate audience), informing the public, on a matter of public interest; texts first published on or after 2 August 2026 count even if generated earlier.

A50-P-04B-S03 (observation; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-35): For each sampled in-scope text: a clear label perceivable without tools (for signatories above the text, near the headline or in the colophon; partial labels allowed for AI parts), or exception evidence.

A50-P-04B-S04 (inspection; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-37, EV-A50-38): Test exception evidence: substantive human review including fact-checking or editorial control with authority to approve, alter or reject; not superficial, automated or cursory checks; editorial responsibility held and its identity and contact published. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04B-S05 (reperformance; sampling SR-A50-06; evidence EV-A50-38): Compare the published version with the signed-off version: any substantive AI change after sign-off voids the exception. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.

A50-P-04B-S06 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-37): Inspect the editorial policy (for non-media signatories: named person with editorial responsibility, organisational measures and resources) or the existing editorial procedures of media service providers. Perform only where the classification answers yes to "Exception relied on: human review or editorial control with editorial responsibility"; where it answers no, record the step as not performed with that reason; an unknown answer is resolved first.
A50-P-04B-S07 (inspection; evidence EV-A50-11, EV-A50-36): Evaluate accessibility of text labels (A50-P-05) and inspect the internal process and mislabel log as in A50-P-04A-S07.

fail: A50-P-04A-C01 or C02 fails for a channel.
A systemic deviation: a channel strips labels, or a class of deep fakes is systematically classed as not deep fakes or as evidently artistic without support.
Labels rely on machine-readable marks only (point 117).
inconclusive: A criterion straddles its band.
The population cannot be reconstructed: limitation stated.
pass: A50-P-04A-C01 and C02 pass for every channel.
Classification differences are isolated and explained.
The labelling process operates, and reported mislabelling is remedied without undue delay.
procedures.title: Deep-fake disclosure (Art 50(4), first subparagraph, with Art 50(5))

fail: A50-P-04B-C01 fails for a channel.
The exception is claimed on the basis of spell-checks, automated or cursory review, or an editorial policy that is not applied (point 135).
Editorial responsibility not identifiable publicly where the exception is relied on.
inconclusive: A50-P-04B-C01 straddles its band.
Workflow records too incomplete to test the exception: limitation stated.
pass: A50-P-04B-C01 passes for every channel.
Exception claims are supported by substantive review, published editorial responsibility and no post-sign-off AI change.
procedures.title: Disclosure of AI-generated text on matters of public interest (Art 50(4), second subparagraph)
